cards.title: Rewrite Product Titles for the First 70 Characters
cards.summary: Structure Shopping product titles with core product type first, then features, then specifics, and put the brand name last unless you are a market leader.
cards.use_when: Feed title optimization for any Shopping campaign, especially for cold-traffic acquisition where brand recognition is low.

cards.title: Enable Product Ratings to Lift Shopping CTR
cards.summary: Sign up for product ratings, meet the review thresholds, and let star ratings and review counts differentiate your listings pre-click.
cards.use_when: Shopping ads appear alongside competitors and you want higher click-through rate without extra spend.

cards.title: Chase the Top Quality Store Badge by Fixing Five Experience Categories
cards.summary: Improve browsing, purchase, shipping, returns and store rating to earn Google's top quality store badge, which the source associates with higher Shopping ranking and a ~20% performance lift.
cards.use_when: Merchant Center store-level optimization to raise Shopping ad ranking and CTR without increasing ad spend.

cards.title: Write Shopping Product Titles: Core Type → Features/Benefits → Specifics → Brand
cards.summary: Structure product titles for Google Shopping as core product type, key features/benefits, specifics (size, quantity, use case), then brand at the end.
cards.use_when: Optimizing the product feed titles that power Shopping/PMax product listings, especially when your brand is not a market leader.

cards.title: Recognize Bad Title Patterns: Brand-First Repetition
cards.summary: Diagnose weak Shopping titles by spotting brand-name repetition and absent specification detail across categories.
cards.use_when: Auditing an existing product feed before a Shopping campaign launch or when CTR is low on well-funded listings.

cards.title: Product Image Standards: Resolution, Focus, No Overlays
cards.summary: Meet Google Shopping image requirements and avoid policy violations by keeping images high-resolution, product-focused and free of text overlays.
cards.use_when: Preparing or refreshing Merchant Center imagery for apparel, home goods or any feed flagged for disapprovals.

cards.title: Test Lifestyle and AI Backgrounds Against Plain Product Shots
cards.summary: Lifestyle or elevated/AI-generated backgrounds frequently beat plain white backgrounds on Shopping CTR, so test them SKU by SKU.
cards.use_when: Improving Shopping listing creative when click-through rate is the bottleneck and price/title are already competitive.

cards.title: Write Product Descriptions That Answer Buyer Objections
cards.summary: Use the up to 5,000-character description field to answer real pre-purchase questions in scannable, keyword-relevant copy — never keyword-stuffed.
cards.use_when: Building or cleaning the description attribute in your Merchant Center feed before scaling Shopping spend.

cards.title: Focus Feed Optimization on Price, Title and Image
cards.summary: In Shopping you cannot choose the queries you serve, so direct roughly 95% of feed effort into price, product title and product image.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to spend merchandising effort when Shopping performance is weak and you cannot manipulate query targeting.

cards.title: Set Up a Standard Shopping Campaign (Not PMax)
cards.summary: Configure a standard Shopping campaign with sales objective, purchases-only conversion goal and presence-only location targeting.
cards.use_when: Launching a DTC store's first Shopping campaign in Google Ads.

cards.title: Segment Branded and Non-Branded Shopping Campaigns with Priority Rules
cards.summary: Run a high-priority non-branded Shopping campaign with brand negatives and a low-priority branded campaign to capture branded traffic and block competitors.
cards.use_when: Structuring Shopping campaigns so branded and non-branded performance can be measured separately and competitors can't intercept your brand traffic.

cards.title: Use Shopping Competitive Metrics to Diagnose Why Ads Didn't Serve
cards.summary: Read search impression share, search lost (budget) and search lost (rank) together to explain under-delivery and decide whether to raise budget or bids.
cards.use_when: Weekly Shopping optimization reviews where a campaign hits its ROAS or CPA target but you suspect missed volume.

cards.title: Mine Search Terms and Split Negative Keyword Levels
cards.summary: Review Shopping search term reports frequently, negate irrelevant queries, and fix the feed issue that caused them.
cards.use_when: Weekly optimization of Shopping campaigns, especially in the first weeks after launch or after adding new SKUs.

cards.title: Consolidate Shopping Campaigns Around Best Sellers for Small Accounts
cards.summary: New and mid-sized accounts should concentrate budget on best sellers rather than segmenting thinly; only split out top performers when they are starved of spend.
cards.use_when: Deciding account structure and budget allocation for a DTC store spending roughly 50k–500k per month, or launching a new Shopping account.

cards.title: Choose Manual Bidding for New Shopping Accounts, Target ROAS After ~30–50 Monthly Conversions
cards.summary: Start with Manual CPC or Maximise Clicks without conversion history, then move to Target ROAS and set the target at or slightly below actual ROAS.
cards.use_when: Choosing or changing bid strategy for a Shopping campaign based on how much conversion data the account has.

cards.title: Set Up a Sales-Objective Search Campaign
cards.summary: Configure a non-branded DTC search campaign with purchases-only conversion goal, Search-only networks and presence-only geo targeting.
cards.use_when: Launching or rebuilding text search campaigns for a DTC store in Google Ads.

cards.title: Build RSA Assets with Variety, Not Padding
cards.summary: Populate responsive search ads with distinct headlines, descriptions and extensions so Google can test genuinely different messaging combinations.
cards.use_when: Writing search ad copy for a new or existing search campaign.

cards.title: Set and scale Google Ads campaign budgets safely
cards.summary: Understand average daily budget vs total spend, ignore unreliable forecasts, and scale in controlled increments.
cards.use_when: Launching a new Google Ads search campaign or increasing budget on an existing one.

cards.title: Choose keyword match types by account maturity and goal
cards.summary: Match type selection depends on conversion data and whether you prioritize efficiency or growth.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to add exact, phrase or broad keywords to a search campaign.

cards.title: Classify keywords into four funnel types before targeting
cards.summary: Informational, commercial, transactional and navigational keywords require different landing destinations.
cards.use_when: Planning keyword lists and choosing where each keyword's traffic should land.

cards.title: Run the seed-expand-segment keyword research method
cards.summary: Build 20-30 seed keywords, expand each into long-tail variants, then segment by theme into ad groups.
cards.use_when: Building or rebuilding a search campaign keyword list for a DTC product.

cards.title: Use Keyword Planner, Semrush and ChatGPT for keyword ideation
cards.summary: Three complementary sources for finding long-tail keyword candidates.
cards.use_when: Generating more long-tail keyword ideas after you've defined your seed keywords.

cards.title: Apply negative keyword match types correctly
cards.summary: Broad, phrase and exact negative keywords block different amounts of traffic — choose deliberately.
cards.use_when: Filtering irrelevant search terms out of a search or shopping campaign to cut wasted spend.

cards.title: Choose negative keyword level and review cadence
cards.summary: Apply negatives at account, campaign or ad-group level and review search term reports frequently while accounts are new.
cards.use_when: Setting up a negative keyword structure or deciding how often to review search term reports.

cards.title: Use quality score to understand ad rank and CPC
cards.summary: Quality score (1-10) drives ad rank and CPC via expected CTR, ad relevance and landing page experience.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing why the same keyword costs far more than competitors or planning account improvements.

cards.title: Improve quality score via three levers
cards.summary: Concrete actions to raise expected CTR, ad relevance and landing page experience.
cards.use_when: Working on a low quality score keyword or preparing a new search campaign for competitive terms.

cards.title: Build single theme asset groups (STAGs) instead of mixed ad groups
cards.summary: Tightly themed ad groups keep keyword, ad copy and landing page congruent, raising quality score and lowering CPC.
cards.use_when: Restructuring an existing search campaign or building a new one where keywords have divergent intents.

cards.title: Size ad groups with 2-8 keywords to preserve relevance
cards.summary: Keep each ad group to a handful of closely related keywords rather than stuffing in dissimilar terms.
cards.use_when: Segmenting keyword lists into ad groups for a search campaign.

cards.title: Write headlines that grab, match intent and drive action
cards.summary: Headlines (30 characters) should hook, match the query and include a CTA, using specific formatting conventions.
cards.use_when: Writing or testing RSA headlines for a search campaign.

cards.title: Write descriptions to close, handle objections and build trust
cards.summary: Use the 90-character descriptions to elaborate, reduce risk and add urgency or proof.
cards.use_when: Drafting RSA descriptions for a search campaign.

cards.title: Avoid maxing out and pinning RSA assets
cards.summary: Limit headlines and avoid pinning unless you have a specific reason, to preserve learning and testing.
cards.use_when: Building or revising a responsive search ad.

cards.title: Test RSAs with 7–9 Headlines, Not Always 15
cards.summary: Start responsive search ads with roughly 7–9 headlines to get faster clickthrough-rate readouts instead of maxing the 15-headline cap.
cards.use_when: Building or refreshing responsive search ads for a search campaign and deciding how many headline and description variants to write.

cards.title: Five Ad Assets That Expand Search Real Estate
cards.summary: Use sitelinks, callouts, promotions, price assets and structured snippets to occupy more SERP space and lift CTR at no added media cost.
cards.use_when: Finalizing search ad assets for a campaign and choosing which extensions to add for a product category or store.

cards.title: Bid Strategy Progression for New vs Existing Accounts
cards.summary: Start new Google Ads accounts on manual bidding to gather conversions, then move to value-based automated bidding once conversion volume supports it.
cards.use_when: Choosing a bid strategy for a new or recently relaunched account, or planning when to switch a store's search campaigns to automated bidding.

cards.title: Set Target ROAS At or Below Historical Actuals
cards.summary: Set an initial target ROAS at or slightly under recent actual ROAS so the algorithm can spend and learn before you tighten efficiency.
cards.use_when: Moving a store's campaign from maximize conversion value to target ROAS bidding, or when a target-ROAS campaign has stopped spending.

cards.title: Check Google Can Read Your Site Before Running DSA
cards.summary: Run your target pages through Keyword Planner to confirm Google interprets the products before spending on dynamic search ads.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether dynamic search ads are viable for a store, or diagnosing poor DSA relevance.

cards.title: Configure DSA Targets and Negatives by Category
cards.summary: Segment DSA ad groups by product theme and block non-commercial pages to avoid wasted spend on irrelevant queries.
cards.use_when: Setting up or cleaning up dynamic search ads for a multi-category store.

cards.title: Use DSA as a Test Proxy for Performance Max Search
cards.summary: Test search behavior with DSA before committing budget to Performance Max, since the search component behaves similarly.
cards.use_when: Planning a move into Performance Max or deciding whether to run DSA first for a store.

cards.title: Decide Whether to Run Branded Search
cards.summary: Run branded search campaigns when competitors bid on your brand or you need early conversion data, and skip them when you already dominate organic with no competition.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to allocate budget to a branded search campaign for a store.

cards.title: Branded Search Ad Copy, Bidding and 90% Impression Share
cards.summary: Use manual CPC, pin the brand in headline one and target 90%+ impression share on branded search so competitors cannot take bottom-funnel clicks.
cards.use_when: Setting up copy, bids and targets for a branded search campaign.

cards.title: Performance Max Basic Setup for Ecommerce
cards.summary: Configure Performance Max for purchase value, exclude your brand and hand it clean assets and first-party signals.
cards.use_when: Launching a Performance Max campaign for an ecommerce store.

cards.title: Performance Max Budget, Search Themes and Audience Signals
cards.summary: Set a PMax daily budget of at least 3x average CPA and use first-party customer lists as the main signal.
cards.use_when: Sizing budget and configuring signals at Performance Max launch for a store.

cards.title: Performance Max Learning Phase and Bid Progression
cards.summary: Give Performance Max 4–6 weeks and move from maximize conversion value to target ROAS once it reaches about 50 conversions per month.
cards.use_when: Managing an early-stage Performance Max campaign and deciding when to change bid strategy.

cards.title: Ongoing Performance Max Optimization Checklist
cards.summary: Review search terms, negatives, channel mix, audiences and assets on a regular cadence because PMax is not set-and-forget.
cards.use_when: Running weekly or monthly optimization on a Performance Max campaign for a store.

cards.title: Choose One or Two Performance Max Campaigns Over Sprawl
cards.summary: Consolidate PMax into one campaign with themed asset groups until budget allocation clearly justifies splitting out a scaling campaign.
cards.use_when: Structuring a store's Performance Max campaigns when deciding between consolidation and segmentation.

cards.title: Demand Gen for Remarketing to Cart Abandoners
cards.summary: Build remarketing with Demand Gen rather than Display, optimizing for purchases and targeting cart abandoners.
cards.use_when: Setting up a remarketing campaign to recover abandoned carts for an ecommerce store.

cards.title: Demand Gen remarketing setup for cart abandoners
cards.summary: Step-by-step Google Ads Demand Gen campaign configuration for retargeting imported cart-abandoner audiences with purchases as the conversion goal.
cards.use_when: Setting up a Google Ads retargeting campaign aimed at shoppers who added to cart but did not buy.

cards.title: Five objections that explain cart abandonment and how to answer them in ads
cards.summary: A five-bucket framework for diagnosing why shoppers abandon carts and matching each objection to specific remarketing ad creative.
cards.use_when: Writing retargeting ad creative or offer copy for cart abandoners, and choosing which objection to lead with.

cards.title: Is YouTube a fit for your store? Four prerequisites
cards.summary: Qualifying criteria (AOV, demonstrability, patience, existing winning Meta creative) to check before committing to YouTube ads.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to add or launch a YouTube/Demand Gen channel for a DTC store.

cards.title: YouTube campaign configuration: Demand Gen, Shorts only, maximise conversions
cards.summary: How to configure a Demand Gen YouTube campaign (post Video Action deprecation) to run Shorts-only with mobile devices and learning-phase bidding.
cards.use_when: Launching a YouTube prospecting campaign and choosing channels, devices, bidding and budget.

cards.title: Start narrow and expand horizontally on YouTube targeting
cards.summary: Why the source rejects Meta-style broad targeting on YouTube and instead builds three narrow audiences per product/avatar.
cards.use_when: Building audience targeting for a new YouTube or Demand Gen prospecting campaign.

cards.title: YouTube Shorts creative specs and storytelling structure
cards.summary: Length, format, subtitle and hook-to-CTA structure for YouTube Shorts ads, tested first on Meta.
cards.use_when: Producing video creative for a YouTube Shorts or Demand Gen prospecting campaign.

cards.title: YouTube retargeting campaign with low-level spend
cards.summary: A separate no-guidance video-views campaign for retargeting warm audiences, with keyword/topic exclusions and CPV bidding.
cards.use_when: Adding a retargeting layer to a YouTube prospecting campaign for website visitors or cart abandoners.

cards.title: Three things YouTube-winning brands do
cards.summary: The patterns the source says separate brands succeeding on YouTube from those wasting spend.
cards.use_when: Auditing whether your store is ready for YouTube ads and reviewing your playbook priorities.

cards.title: Demand Gen image ad anatomy for remarketing
cards.summary: Front-end fields to complete in a Demand Gen image ad and how to use headlines/descriptions for offer and objection handling.
cards.use_when: Building or reviewing the asset group for a Demand Gen remarketing campaign.

cards.title: Turn remarketing objection-learning into funnel-wide improvements
cards.summary: Use cart-abandoner retargeting as a testing ground, then push winning objection-handling into upper-funnel creative to reduce abandonment before it happens.
cards.use_when: Iterating on creative across a Google Ads account and trying to raise on-site conversion rate and ROAS.

cards.title: Reconcile Google remarketing with your Meta team
cards.summary: Cross-channel practice of sharing creative learnings between Google and Meta to make remarketing more effective on both.
cards.use_when: Coordinating paid social and paid search teams on retargeting creative and messaging.

cards.title: Launch order for an ecommerce Google Ads account
cards.summary: Sequence campaign types bottom-funnel first (Search/Shopping), then remarketing/PMax, then Demand Gen top-funnel last.
cards.use_when: Planning which campaign types to launch first for a new or restructured ecommerce Google Ads account.

cards.title: Separate branded vs non-branded campaigns
cards.summary: Never mix branded and non-branded targeting in one campaign — split for new-customer acquisition, clean attribution, and correct algorithm signals.
cards.use_when: Structuring new Search or Shopping campaigns, or diagnosing muddled attribution and inflated metrics in an ecommerce account.

cards.title: Bid strategy progression: clicks first, then conversions
cards.summary: Start new accounts on Maximize Clicks to gather conversion data, then switch to Maximize Conversion Value or Target ROAS after enough conversions.
cards.use_when: Setting or reviewing bid strategy on a new ecommerce Google Ads account or one with too few conversions for smart bidding.

cards.title: Use branded campaigns as cheap algorithm training data
cards.summary: Run low-budget branded Search/Shopping to supply Google cheap, high-quality conversion data that accelerates learning in non-branded campaigns.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to bid on your own brand terms in ecommerce Google Ads.

cards.title: Turn off Search Partners and Display Network for Search campaigns
cards.summary: Uncheck search partners and the Google Display Network in Search campaign settings to protect conversion quality.
cards.use_when: Configuring settings for a new ecommerce Search campaign, before launch.

cards.title: Set location targeting to presence, not presence-or-interest
cards.summary: Use 'presence' location targeting so ads only serve people actually in the target country, not those merely interested in it.
cards.use_when: Configuring geographic targeting on any ecommerce Google Ads campaign, especially when selling only to specific countries.

cards.title: Ignore Google's AI keyword and asset generation
cards.summary: Skip Google's automated keyword/asset generation during campaign setup — Google optimizes for its own revenue, not yours, and does not know your brand.
cards.use_when: Building new Search campaigns and facing Google's prompted tools or recommendations.

cards.title: Step 2: add remarketing to re-engage non-converting visitors
cards.summary: Build direct remarketing campaigns (video and display) targeting site visitors who added to cart or began checkout but did not purchase.
cards.use_when: After initial Search/Shopping campaigns are running and you want to recover near-converting traffic in an ecommerce store.

cards.title: Use Performance Max correctly, or use feed-only PMax as a feed-led alternative
cards.summary: Test a feed-led retail PMax configuration against the store baseline without assuming strict audience or channel isolation.
cards.use_when: Evaluating a feed-led versus full-asset Performance Max campaign for an ecommerce product catalog.

cards.title: Introduce Demand Gen last, for top-of-funnel cold traffic
cards.summary: Use Demand Gen (video-only or all-assets) for cold audiences only after bottom and mid-funnel campaigns are saturated.
cards.use_when: Deciding when and how to run cold top-of-funnel Google Ads for an ecommerce brand.

cards.title: Link Shopify and Merchant Center, then Merchant Center to Google Ads
cards.summary: Three-way linking (Shopify → Google Merchant Center → Google Ads) is the prerequisite for any Shopping or feed-based campaign.
cards.use_when: Preparing an ecommerce store to run Shopping or feed-based Google Ads for the first time.

cards.title: Feed product titles with informative keywords
cards.summary: Write Merchant Center product titles that include the full product name, key attributes, and brand so Google matches them to the right searches.
cards.use_when: Optimizing Merchant Center product data before running Shopping campaigns.

cards.title: Product descriptions: use AI for keyword-rich copy, but never wrong attributes
cards.summary: Generate long Merchant Center descriptions with a tool like ChatGPT, but exclude any attribute the product does not actually have.
cards.use_when: Filling Merchant Center product description fields across a catalog without hand-writing every one.

cards.title: Use feed management tools for large catalogs
cards.summary: For large product catalogs, use a feed management app rather than editing every Merchant Center field manually.
cards.use_when: Working with a large SKU count and standard Shopify–Merchant Center sync is too slow or limited.

cards.title: Configure Shopping campaign objective and conversions
cards.summary: In Shopping campaign setup, select the sales objective and use only the purchase conversion goal — not add to cart or begin checkout.
cards.use_when: Creating a Shopping campaign for an ecommerce store and choosing conversion goals.

cards.title: Use Search for category/collection intent, Shopping for specific products
cards.summary: Route broad category searches to Search campaigns pointed at collection pages, and specific-product searches to Shopping listings.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether a keyword should be covered by a Search campaign or left to Shopping listings in an ecommerce account.

cards.title: Write branded vs non-branded Search ad copy
cards.summary: Include the brand name and pin it first in branded ads; emphasize range and guarantees in non-branded category ads.
cards.use_when: Writing RSA headlines and assets for branded or non-branded ecommerce Search campaigns.

cards.title: Fill out ad extensions to expand ad real estate
cards.summary: Use sitelinks, callouts, structured snippets, promotions, prices, business name and logo to enlarge ads, build trust and lift CTR.
cards.use_when: Building Search ad assets for an ecommerce campaign and trying to maximize click-through rate.

cards.title: Set branded and category Search budgets
cards.summary: Keep branded budgets modest ($10–$50/day typical) and test category Search campaigns at roughly $20–$30/day based on AOV.
cards.use_when: Allocating daily budget to branded vs category Search campaigns for an ecommerce store.

cards.title: Use negative keywords to protect non-branded campaigns
cards.summary: Add your brand terms as negatives in every non-branded campaign to stop branded searches leaking in and inflating metrics.
cards.use_when: Building or auditing non-branded Search or Shopping campaigns in an ecommerce account.

cards.title: Test category Search campaigns cautiously
cards.summary: Non-branded category Search campaigns are optional in ecommerce — only launch them when a popular category shows likely profitable demand.
cards.use_when: Evaluating whether to add non-branded category Search campaigns alongside Shopping.

cards.title: Set up a first Standard Shopping campaign for bestsellers only
cards.summary: Launch Google Shopping by running only 5-10 bestseller products in a single ad group instead of dumping the whole catalog in one campaign.
cards.use_when: You are creating your first Google Shopping campaign and deciding which products to advertise.

cards.title: Restrict a Shopping ad group to specific products by item ID
cards.summary: Use product group subdivisions and exclusion to make a bestsellers ad group run only the chosen products, not the whole feed.
cards.use_when: Your new Shopping ad group is showing all products and you want it to contain only bestsellers.
